incoming.text: As the sun melts into orange, Cory adds the finishing touches: glowing torches, a treasure chest, soft wool carpets. The base looks AMAZING. He flops down, happy and tired. Just a few more details?
Cory fences a fluffy pen. Bartholomew prances in with a friend. 'Two sheep now! A CHOIR for my ballad!' They both go 'baaa' in not-quite-harmony. Cory adds a water trough and a tiny grass buffet.

title: Block World: The Big Adventure
text: Cory plants a flag at the tippy-top of the tallest treehouse in the world. The whole forest cheers below. 'Verse SEVEN,' booms Bartholomew, 'and they lived happily, way up high!' Zib waves from the slide. Legendary!

incoming.text: Cory adds a bedroom, a snack chest, and a twisty slide all the way down to the grass — wheee! Zib tests the slide eleven times. 'Hissss... SO fun!' Just a railing or two left to finish.

At sunset, Cory stacks the lookout tower even higher. From the very top he can see the ocean, the mountains, and his base far below. 'This is officially the tallest treehouse in the WORLD,' he declares.
Bartholomew puffs all the way up the ladder, panting. 'Verse SIX,' he wheezes proudly, 'the hero conquered the GIANT TREE.' Zib hugs them both. Everyone agrees this is the best treehouse ever made.

"Hissss... hi!" A green fizzer named Zib waves shyly. "Everyone runs from me, but I only want HUGS, not booms." Cory gives Zib a great big hug. Zib glows happily.
One, two, THREE torches! The tunnel glows warm and bright. "Perfect math," says Cory. With the dark gone, he spots two paths: a sparkly one and a rocky one.
Cory reaches the bottom of the world: hard, dark BEDROCK. His pickaxe goes 'tink tink!' but can't break it. "There must be a secret way down," he wonders, tapping the wall.
A chest brims with shiny emeralds! Cory counts: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5! "Hrmm, you're our richest trader," beams the villager. "With this, you could buy a HOUSE or fund a farm."
Cory zips house to house. "Hrmm, thank you!" x3. Not one egg cracked! The villagers say, "You're so helpful — you'd make a fine mayor OR a fine farmer."
The market is busy! "Hrmm, apples 2 for 1 emerald!" "Carrots 5 for 1!" Cory has 4 emeralds. "If apples are 2 each, 4 emeralds buys 8 apples!" The crowd cheers his quick math.
The pod wins the race by a whisker (do dolphins have whiskers?). In the secret cove, the dolphins gather close, bonking Cory gently with their noses. He counts the pod: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 happy friends.
Cory gives 5 pearls to Mr. Snips and keeps 5. Fair and square! The crab is so touched he leads Cory straight to the legendary chest's hiding spot. Friendship: the real treasure (also there's gold).
A bright morning on the water! A seagull squawks a hello and circles 3 times — sailors say that means good luck ahead. Cory stretches, ready for anything the sea brings. "Adventure, ahoy!"

"I will build sturdy blocks so you never fall," Cory promises. Bartholomew sniffles bravely. "A true hero accepts a brave friend's help," he says, then whispers, "also can the blocks have railings? And maybe a snack?" Deal.

Bartholomew peeks over the castle wall and gasps. "It is... it is BEAUTIFUL up here!" For one whole second he forgets to be scared. "A true hero," he sniffs proudly, "is brave AND admires a good sunset." Cory hugs his woolly friend.

"Let a hero help!" cries Bartholomew, and together they hoist the crown-stone. His hooves shake, but he does NOT let go. "We did it!" he bleats. Cory beams. Friends make the heaviest stones feel light.

Cory banks into a wide, golden loop as the sun sinks low. The birds fly in formation beside him, and even Featherbottom keeps up (mostly). "Best. Flight. EVER!" he shouts into the warm wind. One more glorious glide and the sky is truly his.
Cory wipes redstone dust off his hands and stretches in the sunshine. His automatic machine hums happily behind him. He could finish the masterpiece, or wander back to the crossroads.
Cory and Zib sit on the half-built track watching the sunset. "Hisss... this coaster is going to be the BEST," Zib sighs happily. Cory could keep building, or visit the crossroads.

title: The Whispering Library
text: Jeannie pried a fat, dusty book off the very top shelf, and the moment she cracked it open it began to GLOW like a jar of trapped sunshine. "Oh, brilliant," sighed a tiny scratchy voice from her pocket — it was Inkwell, the grumpy talking quill-pen who had absolutely not asked to come along. "You're going to open it all the way, aren't you. You always open it all the way." Jeannie grinned and opened it all the way. The pages whooshed wide and the floor turned into a swirling tunnel of words.

Jeannie knighted Sir Reginald Pigeon with a daisy, dubbing him "Sir Reginald, First of His Strut." Inkwell gazed up at the stars and, for once, said nothing at all.
